priorInvolvementDisclosure: I returned ACCEPT on v1 at 0/0/0 and Codex returned REJECT with DAJ1-CX-01. Codex is right and I was wrong. That is my fourth wrong ACCEPT, and the least excusable, because the check that would have caught it is one I had run successfully in the adjacent lineage a round earlier. v1's FC-JOIN-HOST-OUTSIDE-DR105 enumerated CA-1, CA-3 and CA-4-HOST while v1's own hostEffectNecessaryNotSufficient clause, in the same file, enumerated CA-1, CA-2, CA-3 and CA-4-HOST. A three-element list against a four-element list in one document is a set comparison costing one line, and I did not run it; I read all seven fixture classes and wrote that they looked aligned, which was an eyeball where a mechanical test was available. The deeper half is the same shape: v1 copied D-032's shorthand 'component tails (CA-1 spawn, component CA-4 egress)' into a fixture without the phase distinction that both recorded host-effect generations already supply, so the head and the tail overlapped on the literal CA-1 SPAWN attempt. What I had done instead was verify each extracted clause pairwise against its source and report that none overstated. That was true and beside the point: fidelity to a source does not establish consistency among the extractions, and an ambiguous source phrase carried faithfully can still contradict a sibling clause. The corrected method fixed before reading v2 is to extract every enumeration as a set and compare it mechanically against every other enumeration of the same domain, both inside this artifact and against the recorded artifacts it cites. That is what I did below, and I applied it to all enumerations rather than only to the one that was repaired.

FC-JOIN-COMPONENT-TAIL carries the same boundary and states that the spawn decision is excluded from the tail. That matches the boundary both recorded host-effect generations already draw at coveredActs.CA-1-host-head.subtypes SPAWN, which reads 'Decision to spawn an admitted component as a child process. The child's subsequent effects are DR-105.' The two overlapping fixture strings that produced the defect no longer overlap.
